description: Capability for the popover window. Kept minimal — the popover is render-only and never spawns processes or reads the filesystem directly; it talks to Rust exclusively through get_state()/refresh_now/hide_popover/state-changed/open_settings_window/check_for_update/apply_update. T8/F3 (sec review, tightened again for T9 D2), M2/S6 (one further addition), M4/S5 (check_for_update/apply_update): scoped to exactly the IPC surface src/ actually calls, not the broad core:default bundle — core:event:allow-listen for the state-changed subscription AND the window focus/blur events onFocusChanged listens to (both delivered over the SAME generic event-listen permission, no separate core:window:* grant needed), plus the app commands (auto-generated by build.rs's AppManifest, see permissions/autogenerated/). allow-hide-popover is the one addition for D2 (Esc / click-outside dismiss) — still just a hide, not a general window-control grant: no show/focus/move/resize/close-window permission exists here, and no fs/shell/http/dialog plugin is linked at all. Opening the popover remains Rust-only (tray click handler / CT_SHOW_POPOVER_ON_LAUNCH test hook); the webview can only ever ask Rust to hide it, never show it. allow-open-settings-window (M2/S7's footer 'Preferences…' row, S6) is the one Settings-surface grant the popover needs — it does NOT get allow-get-settings/allow-save-settings (those are scoped to capabilities/settings.json, the Settings window's own capability, least-privilege — the popover never reads or writes the layer manifest itself). allow-check-for-update/allow-apply-update (M4/S5, render/update.ts's self-update banner, `.copilot/wp/24.md`) are the ONLY two commands granting the popover any network/filesystem-adjacent capability at all — and even those are Rust-side-only: the webview never gets a fs/shell/http/dialog plugin grant of its own, it only ever asks Rust to run the already-fail-closed fetch/verify/stage pipeline (`updater::check`) and reports back a plain DTO.
